elements.problem: Sudden + severe + at rest leg pain is one qualified finding (all three qualifiers present) AND any of numbness, weakness, pallor, no pulse. Logic (and + or) matches the page. Pallor is 'White discoloration of skin' with finding_site Lower limb structure: SNOMED has no pallor-of-limb concept ('Pallor' as a finding does not exist), so this is an acceptable construction. All concepts exist and are checked for in the same form.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent leg symptom conditions (check_for) / Diagnose probable DVT (leg symptoms)
rule_level_problems.problem: The red box's DVT risk factors (BMI > 30, smoker, immobile, pregnant, on oestrogen, leg trauma, recent hospitalisation, TB, cancer) are absent from the check_for and from every rule. summary: The DVT red-box item is only partly captured: 'swelling and pain in one calf' is encoded correctly but none of the nine 'especially if' risk factors (BMI > 30, smoker, immobile, pregnant, oestrogen, leg trauma, recent hospitalisation, TB, cancer) is checked for or used, against the house rule that every red-box item is in the check_for. The sciatica box's same-day red flags (retention/incontinence, saddle numbness, leg weakness, difficulty walking) and the both-legs-swollen/no-orthopnoea branch (pregnancy, dipstick blood or protein) are not encoded; both are borderline scope. Everything else on the page is encoded correctly: all four red-box 'likely' diagnoses, the Urgent priority built from them, and the six flowchart conclusions (joint problem, sciatica, PVD, heart failure, sprain, strain) use existing SNOMED concepts with the page's and/or logic, with only low-severity overlaps (PVD not excluding CLI findings; sprain/strain not excluding inability to bear weight).
